headline: Overseas acquirers paying a 32% premium over domestic buyers for Australian companies, though record ASX levels and AUD may temper foreign interest
reasoning: Simon James notes that international buyers paid a 32% premium compared to Australian-based acquirers in the prior year, which is a significant differential. However, he flags that Australian stock markets are at record highs and the Australian dollar's current level may reduce the attractiveness of Australian targets for foreign buyers. He also notes that taking out an ASX-listed company is more operationally complex and capital-intensive than comparable processes in other markets like the UK.
quote: Australian stock markets kind of record highs. Um, the dollars where it is, is it as attractive for a foreign company to come in and and take out Aussie companies. Maybe. Maybe not. I think the data that we saw international buyers last year were paying a it worked out at like a 32% premium versus any of the transactions that were Australian based, which is, you know, a significant amount of money. If overseas is going to pay 32% more, let's sell to overseas.

headline: AI-driven productivity gains expected to fuel acquisition of legacy businesses as companies seek to capture margin rather than cut prices
reasoning: Simon James observes that many businesses are integrating AI into their supply chains and making significant headway. He argues that instead of passing productivity savings on to customers via price cuts, the smarter play is to acquire legacy businesses and push AI-driven productivity gains into those businesses, keeping prices stable, capturing the margin improvement, and achieving a quicker payback. This dynamic is expected to drive a new wave of M&A with an AI arbitrage thesis.
quote: I speak to lots of businesses kind of every day when you're talking to businesses, especially how they're kind of putting AI through their supply chain and how they're looking to do that. Lots of organizations are making big headway in that space. And it's a case of, are we going to keep that as a competitive advantage? Maybe we drop our prices to gain market share, but I think the bigger play will be actually, let's keep our prices where they are. Let's buy some legacy businesses and push those productivity gains and our knowhow into those legacy businesses and keep prices up and take that margin for ourselves and get a quicker payback.

headline: M&A transaction volumes in Australia down ~17% year-on-year as buyers sit on their hands despite ample dry powder
reasoning: Simon James notes that deal volumes have fallen about 17% compared to last year, with buyers being more selective despite strong structural incentives to deploy capital. Average transaction values have risen from A$133m to A$162m, and average multiples paid have increased from 9.9x to 10.5x. He argues there is significant dry capital within private equity, listed companies, and private capital sectors that is yet to be deployed. The combination of high stock prices offering multiple arbitrage and abundant capital makes the subdued activity surprising.
quote: Numbers are down about 17% on transaction volumes compared to last year. Buyers have just been a lot more selective. There's lots of opportunities out there, but for some reason, buyers are just sitting on their hands. Um, there's a lot of market forces pointing to why buyer should be buying. Uh, stock prices are high so they can get multiple arbitrage by buying low. And but they just don't know sitting on their hands a little bit.

headline: Australian tax reform changes expected to accelerate M&A activity before June next year as baby boomers rush to transact
reasoning: Simon James highlights that proposed tax changes — including a 50% tax on extra capital gains — are likely to accelerate deal activity, particularly among baby boomers looking to retire and exit private businesses rather than pass them to family. He expects generational wealth transfer from private businesses to drive a wave of deal flow in the period leading up to June next year as owners seek to transact before the new regime kicks in.
quote: With the tax changes, I think there's probably going to be a lot more acceleration between now and June next year. Uh, so people just kind of wanting to, to kind of transact and move, move a bit faster. What are we seeing with baby boomers at the moment? That end of the market, I guess, you know, heading to retirement, succession planning or adjusting a portfolio. Worried about how much tax they're going to pay. They're going to be paying 50% tax on any extra gains. So that's definitely going to accelerate some things.
